newsitem.title: SPAIN: Firms win Spanish airport cargo handling tenders.
newsitem.headline: Firms win Spanish airport cargo handling tenders.

text.p: Two groups of companies have won the contest to compete with flag carrier Iberia in handling services at three major Spanish airports, the airports authority (AENA) said.
A consortium formed by Ineuropa, Frankfurt Airport and construction companies Cubiertas and Entrecanales will provide passenger and ramp services at Madrid's Barajas airport from April next year.

A group formed by building firm FCC, Agua y Entorno Urbano and Air Espana, parent company of Iberia's airline competitor Air Europa, has won the tender for passenger and ramp services at Barcelona and for passenger, ramp and cargo services at Malaga airport.
Cargo services at Madrid and Barcelona were awarded to a second operator, a group formed by Aldeasa and Ogden Skycare, in 1995, an AENA spokeswoman said.
These contracts complete the process of liberalising handling at Spain's main airports begun in 1993.
Seven groups bid for the concession at each of the three awarded this week.
Barajas handled more than 16 million passengers in the first nine months of this year and 174,197 tonnes of cargo, followed by Barcelona with 10 million passengers and 56,280 tonnes of cargo.
Iberia, until this year the sole handling provider, earned just over 55 billion pesetas from handling services in 1995.
